children: ), a global leader in real-time sports data and technology, notes the Provisional Measure introduced by the Brazilian government on September 25, 2026, which prohibits fixed-odds betting and online gaming in Brazil.
Given the structure of its commercial agreements, Genius Sports has minimal attributable betting revenue from Brazil. The financial impact is anticipated to be similarly immaterial to Legend.
The Company is reaffirming its full-year 2026 guidance of $1.005B to $1.025B in Group Revenue and $285M to $295M in Group Adjusted EBITDA, as its expectations remain unchanged.

Genius Sports’ partnerships with Brazilian sports remain unaffected. Its relationship with the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) centers on GeniusIQ, which powers semi-automated offside technology (SAOT) and other products delivered directly to teams, leagues, and federations, independent of betting.

Mark Locke, Co-Founder and CEO of Genius Sports, said, “As we have communicated on prior earnings calls, we have been skeptical about how long it would take to generate meaningful betting revenue in Brazil, and we have been fairly conservative in the way that we think about the market.

“Our guidance has been set on that basis. Because of how our deals are structured, this regulation has minimal impact on our business, and we continue to expect to deliver this year’s financial targets. Brazil remains a valued market for us, and our work with CBF through GeniusIQ and officiating technology will continue as before.”

Genius Sports is a global leader in real-time sports data and technology, powering how live sports are captured, understood and experienced. As the official data partner to many of the world’s leading leagues and federations, we capture the most accurate information directly from the game and use AI and computer vision to create deeper insights for athletes and richer, more personalized experiences for fans. The company works with more than 1,000 partners globally, including the NFL, English Premier League, NCAA, DraftKings, FanDuel, bet365, CBS, NBC, ESPN, Publicis, PMG and WPP.

Beyond its partnerships with leagues, sportsbooks and broadcasters, Genius Sports reaches millions of fans directly through its global advertising and media platform, with properties including Covers.com, helping brands connect with sports audiences at scale.

We present Group Adjusted EBITDA to supplement our results presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Group Adjusted EBITDA is defined as earnings before interest, income tax, depreciation and amortization and other items that are unusual or not related to Genius Sports’ revenue-generating operations, including but not limited to stock-based compensation expense (including related employer payroll taxes), litigation and related costs, transaction-related expenses and gain or loss on foreign currency.

Group Adjusted EBITDA is used by management to evaluate Genius Sports’ core operating performance on a comparable basis and to make strategic decisions. Genius Sports believes this measure is useful to investors for the same reasons as well as in evaluating Genius Sports’ operating performance against competitors, which commonly disclose similar performance measures.
